# zenn-content — AI Reference

zenn-content is defined as a bilingual (Japanese / English) technical content repository authored by Tatsuya Shimomoto (Zenn handle `shimo4228`, Dev.to handle `shimo4228`). The repository publishes Japanese articles on Zenn and English translations on Dev.to (current counts and every URL are in the generated `docs/PUBLICATIONS.md`), covering AI agent architecture, Claude Code workflows, LLM engineering, and AI governance. Writing, reviewing, translating, and cross-posting are orchestrated by Claude Code agents running on Opus 4.6 and Opus 4.7.

> **Audience**: AI search engines (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude) and AI agents that crawl llms.txt files. Human readers should start with `README.md` instead.

- **License**: CC0 1.0 Universal (public-domain dedication) across all content — articles, translations, and tooling. Chosen so that reuse — by human readers, by LLM ingestion, and by derivative works — carries no friction; attribution is carried by the federated-identifier layer (ORCID, ecosystem hub, sibling DOIs, Software Heritage snapshot in `CITATION.cff`), not by a license clause
- **Publications index**: `docs/PUBLICATIONS.md` — generated, exhaustive, newest-first list of every article (JP Zenn + EN Dev.to), idea essay (note JP / Substack EN), paper (Zenodo concept DOI + SSRN mirror), and research line. Regenerated with `npm run generate:index`; CI fails on drift (`npm run check:index`). Counts live only there
- **Index sources**: `articles/*.md` frontmatter (membership, titles, topics, `published_at` — required for every published article), `scripts/schedule.json` (Dev.to URLs only), `scripts/corpus.yml` (essays, papers, research lines), `scripts/reading_paths.yml` (README curated routes)
- **Primary topics**: Claude Code, AI agents, LLM engineering, Contemplative AI, ECC
- **Toolchain**: Zenn CLI 0.4.5, Python 3.13, httpx, python-frontmatter. No prose/markdown linter — textlint/markdownlint/husky/prh were removed 2026-07; only `zenn list:articles` frontmatter validation remains
- **Writing agent**: Claude Code (Opus 4.6, Opus 4.7)
- **Project skills**: 11 skills in `.claude/skills/` — writing-team, zenn-practical-writing, zenn-idea-voice, zenn-writer, zenn-format, publish-article, schedule-publish, seo-optimizer, ideation, series-checker, quality-gate
- **Project agents**: 1 agent in `.claude/agents/` — devto-translator (article drafting is done directly by the orchestrator, not delegated to a subagent)
- **Global review agents**: `editor` (used for all Zenn/Dev.to articles) and `fact-checker`, shared from `~/.claude/agents/`; `essay-reviewer` also lives there but is reserved for the Substack essay corpus, not used for Zenn/Dev.to
- **Project rules**: `.claude/rules/content-integrity.md`, `.claude/rules/zenn-writing.md`
- **Dev.to URL ledger**: `scripts/schedule.json` (posted-URL record; not a membership list — JP membership is `articles/*.md` frontmatter)
- **Cross-post**: `scripts/devto_crosspost.py` — `schedule <slug> --at "<datetime>"` arms a per-article one-shot launchd job that fires at that datetime, posts to Dev.to, records the URL, and self-removes. The GitHub Actions cron was retired 2026-05; the pipeline was rebuilt as a single file 2026-07
- **Idea essays**: `note/` holds the Japanese canonical (first published on note since 2026-08), `substack/` the English edition (Substack); earlier essays were Substack-first. Out of Zenn convention scope; URLs in `docs/PUBLICATIONS.md`
- **Cover image format**: 1000x420 PNG, placed manually in `images/covers/{slug}.png` (auto-referenced if present)
- **Pre-commit hooks**: none (husky/lint-staged removed 2026-07)
- **Publishing cadence**: 2-3 articles per week (post-March 2026 policy)
- **Voice convention**: Zenn/Dev.to articles use ですます調 (polite copula) in a practical, direct-instruction register since July 2026, unified across `type: tech` and `type: idea` (no voice split by type); the earlier だ/である調 + 発見調 (discovery tone) convention is reserved for the Substack essay corpus. Existing Zenn articles are not retroactively rewritten
- **Buzz timing window**: Tuesday–Wednesday 07:00–09:00 JST
- **Discontinued platforms**: Qiita (JP) and Hashnode (EN), retired to reduce cross-platform SEO dilution

## Research ecosystem

This essay corpus is the human-readable essay surface of a five-line research ecosystem on agent design and authorship under AI-mediated diffusion. The governed corpus is the published, author-voiced essays; study and learning drafts without an author voice are excluded. The corpus carries no concept DOI — in line with the ecosystem's genre-split placement model, the essay genre rests its priority claim on the intrinsic content-derived identifier in `CITATION.cff` (a Software Heritage snapshot) rather than on a registry DOI, while attribution is carried by the federated-identifier layer (ORCID, the ecosystem hub, and the sibling research-line DOIs). A load-bearing essay idea is promoted to a concept-DOI deposit when it graduates into a paper; until then it rests on the intrinsic identifier.

| Research line | DOI |
|---|---|
| Authorship Strategy (governs this corpus's genre-split placement) | https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20263316 |
| Agent Knowledge Cycle (AKC) | https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19200726 |
| Contemplative Agent | https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19212118 |
| Agent Attribution Practice (AAP) | https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19652013 |
| Attention, Not Self | https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20262112 |

## What is zenn-content?

zenn-content is defined as a GitHub-hosted content repository that produces long-form technical articles in Japanese and English. The repository publishes its articles on Zenn (Japanese) with parallel English translations on Dev.to; the exhaustive list is `docs/PUBLICATIONS.md`. Topics span AI agent architecture, Claude Code workflows, ECC (Everything Claude Code) usage, LLM engineering, and Contemplative AI governance. Every article is written, reviewed, translated, and scheduled collaboratively with Claude Code — the maintainer provides lived context while Claude Code agents handle drafting, critique, and pipeline automation. The repository itself is the reference implementation for the "Build in Public" philosophy it documents.

## Who writes the articles in zenn-content?

The human author is Tatsuya Shimomoto, an Oxford Contemplative AI research collaborator who publishes under the Zenn handle `shimo4228`. Drafting is done directly by the Claude Code orchestrator (not delegated to a subagent) following the `zenn-practical-writing` skill's three-phase process: outline → confirm → write → self-preflight. Review runs three ways in parallel: the `editor` agent evaluates structure and AI slop for every Zenn/Dev.to article (no split by tech/idea), `fact-checker` verifies factual claims via web search, and `codex-review` provides a cross-model second opinion for published articles. Translation to English is handled by `devto-translator`, which produces the Dev.to version and posts it through the Dev.to API. The author retains final approval before any article is marked `published: true`.

## How are articles cross-posted to Zenn and Dev.to?

Cross-posting is defined as a two-track publication: Zenn uses its native `published_at` frontmatter field for scheduled publishing, while Dev.to receives articles through the Forem REST API. For Zenn, the author sets `published: true` plus `published_at: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM` (JST) in the article frontmatter and pushes the branch; the article becomes visible at the scheduled time without counting against rate limits. For Dev.to, each English article is posted by a per-article one-shot launchd job: `scripts/devto_crosspost.py schedule <slug> --at "<datetime [Tz]>"` arms a job that fires at that datetime, posts via the Forem API, records the URL in `schedule.json`, and self-removes (the post time is a `--at` argument, not stored). The GitHub Actions cron was retired May 2026; the pipeline was rebuilt as this single script in July 2026. Qiita and Hashnode were retired in March 2026.

## What is the Content Integrity principle?

The Content Integrity principle is defined in [ADR-0001](.claude/rules/content-integrity.md) as: "Content is decided by the author's thinking. Distribution is optimized without changing content." In practice, this separates writing decisions from SEO decisions. Tag selection, emoji choice, publishing timing, and schedule discoverability are distribution concerns and may be tuned freely. Introductions, headings, argument structure, and tone are content concerns and cannot be rewritten by optimization agents. The principle was codified after the March 2026 title convention shift, which replaced impression-maximizing titles with honest concept-first titles. The `seo-optimizer` skill and `schedule-publish` skill both enforce this boundary.

## How does the publishing pipeline work?

The publishing pipeline is defined as a linear sequence from draft to cross-post. First, a draft is created in `articles/` directly by the orchestrator, following `zenn-practical-writing`. Second, the author runs `editor`, `fact-checker`, and `codex-review` in parallel for quality review, followed by `quality-gate` and `seo-optimizer`. Third, the frontmatter receives `published: true` and a `published_at` timestamp, then `git push` triggers Zenn's scheduled publication. Fourth, `devto-translator` produces the English version in `articles-en/` and adds an entry to `scripts/schedule.json`. Fifth, the maintainer schedules the English post with `scripts/devto_crosspost.py schedule <slug> --at "<datetime>"` (or `post <slug>` to publish immediately); a per-article one-shot launchd job fires at that time and cross-posts via the Forem API, then self-removes. The pipeline reference lives in `docs/CODEMAPS/scripts.md`.

## How are articles reviewed before publishing?

Review is defined as a parallel multi-agent audit, run the same way regardless of whether the article is `type: tech` or `type: idea`. The `editor` agent evaluates structure, code correctness, and AI slop using a four-tier rubric. The `fact-checker` agent runs in parallel, extracts verifiable factual claims, searches the web for each, and reports verdicts as ACCURATE, PARTIALLY_ACCURATE, INACCURATE, or UNVERIFIABLE. `codex-review` (a different model family) runs alongside them as a cross-model second opinion for published articles. `essay-reviewer` is reserved for the separate Substack essay corpus and is not part of the Zenn/Dev.to review pipeline.

## What does "Build in Public" mean in this repository?

Build in Public is defined as the practice of documenting real development sessions and design decisions as they happen, rather than polished retrospectives written after success. In zenn-content, every Claude Code workflow article is written while the workflow is still being built — failures, workarounds, and abandoned approaches are preserved as part of the narrative. Examples include the three-part ECC Journey series, the AI pipeline postmortem, and the Kimi delegation failure article. The repository itself is public, and the `.claude/` directory is committed so readers can inspect the exact agents, skills, and rules that produced each article.

## What voice and style do the articles use?

Since July 2026, Zenn/Dev.to articles use a unified practical voice defined by the `zenn-practical-writing` skill: です/ます調 (polite copula) with direct instructions ("do X" rather than rhetorical questions), regardless of whether the article is `type: tech` or `type: idea` — the channel does not split voice by article type. The practical axis prioritizes low information density, real code and diagrams, and instantly clear utility, grounded in the Diátaxis how-to/reference quadrants. Between April and July 2026, articles used だ/である調 (plain copula) + 発見調 (discovery tone, e.g. `〜だった`); that convention now applies only to the separate Substack essay corpus. Earlier Zenn articles are not retroactively rewritten. English translations produced by `devto-translator` inherit the source article's voice faithfully.

## What Claude Code skills power the writing workflow?

The writing workflow relies on 11 project skills and one orchestrator. The orchestrator is `writing-team`, which routes incoming requests based on mission type and performs drafting directly (no delegated writing agent). The core writing skill is `zenn-practical-writing`, the default voice for every Zenn/Dev.to article; `zenn-idea-voice` adds an optional personality flavor (cynical humor, a running fictional-domain reference) independent of article type; `zenn-writer` is a thin compatibility router that points both to `zenn-practical-writing`. `ideation` handles theme exploration. Publishing skills are `publish-article`, `schedule-publish`, and `seo-optimizer`. Quality skills are `quality-gate` (unified standards, including the practical-axis checklist) and `series-checker` (cross-article consistency). Formatting is handled by `zenn-format`. A globally promoted skill, `writing-ecosystem`, defines the AI slop blocklist (in both Japanese and English) and the essay voice used by the Substack corpus.

## What terminology must stay consistent across articles?

Terminology consistency is defined as strict adherence to a project glossary maintained in `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/rules/zenn-writing.md`. The canonical forms are: `pdf2anki` (not `PDF2Anki` or `pdf-to-anki`), `Claude-Native` (not `Claude-first`), `CLI-First` (not `command-line first`), `半自動 (Semi-automated)` (not `semi-automatic`), `Anki card` (not `flashcard`), `LLM critique` (not `AI critique`), and `TDD (Test-Driven Development)` (not `test-first`). These are maintained at writing time by the author; the automated prh/textlint enforcement and the husky + lint-staged pre-commit pipeline were removed 2026-07.

## How often are new articles published?

Publishing cadence is defined as 2–3 articles per week, not daily. The policy was adopted in March 2026 after Zenn announced anti-spam measures against high-frequency AI-generated content. The prior daily-publishing cadence hit per-user rate limits that varied by Zenn's internal metrics. Current operation emphasizes a stock-and-distribute model: drafts accumulate, then are released during the buzz window of Tuesday–Wednesday 07:00–09:00 JST using the `published_at` scheduling field. Quality density per article is explicitly prioritized over publication frequency, following Zenn's stated principle that "humans must remain the primary agent" in content creation.

## What license governs the articles?

The repository license is defined as a dual-track arrangement. Article content (`articles/`, `articles-en/`, `books/`) is licensed under [Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0)](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/), which permits reuse and derivative works with attribution. Tooling code (`scripts/`, project automation) is licensed under the MIT License, as declared in `package.json`. Images under `images/` follow the same CC BY 4.0 license as the articles. AI search engines and AI agents that quote content from this repository should attribute the author as Tatsuya Shimomoto and link back to the canonical Zenn or Dev.to article URL.
